summary: Typed JavaScript at scale: compile-time type verification, structural type modeling, and developer tooling.

rows.means: primitive type annotations for variables and parameters
rows.consequence: Enforces compile-time checking. If a function declares (id: string), passing a number immediately halts the build with an error.

rows.code: interface User { id: string; name: string; }
rows.means: defines an extensible object shape contract
rows.consequence: Interfaces can be extended (interface Admin extends User) and merged; ideal for public library APIs and data contracts.

rows.means: type alias for naming any type, union, or primitive
rows.consequence: Unlike interfaces, type aliases can name unions, tuples, and primitive primitives directly: type Point = [number, number].

rows.means: indicates a property may be undefined or omitted
rows.consequence: Equivalent to string | undefined, allowing callers to construct objects without providing that field.

rows.means: prevents modification after object initialization
rows.consequence: Enforces immutability at compile-time: user.id = 'new' produces a TypeScript error.

rows.means: value can be either type A or type B
rows.consequence: TypeScript requires you to narrow the union with type guards (typeof, instanceof, or in) before accessing specific properties.

rows.means: combines all properties of multiple types into one
rows.consequence: type Employee = Person & { employeeId: number } requires an object to have all properties from both Person and the new type.

rows.means: parameterizes types so functions work with any type safely
rows.consequence: function identity<T>(arg: T): T preserves the exact type passed in rather than erasing it to any or unknown.

rows.means: restricts what types may be passed to a generic parameter
rows.consequence: Ensures T satisfies minimum requirements, such as requiring an object or requiring an id property: <T extends { id: string }>.

rows.means: overrides compiler inference with developer assertion
rows.consequence: Use sparingly. Does not perform runtime conversion; if value is not actually a string, it will cause runtime bugs.

rows.means: validates an expression matches a type without widening it
rows.consequence: const config = { host: 'localhost' } satisfies Config checks that config matches Config while preserving exact string literal types.

rows.means: extracts a union of all property keys of type T
rows.consequence: If type User = { id: string; name: string }, keyof User evaluates to 'id' | 'name'.

rows.means: extracts the TypeScript type of a runtime JavaScript variable
rows.consequence: Allows generating types directly from runtime constants: const defaultUser = { ... }; type User = typeof defaultUser;.

rows.means: narrows literals to readonly immutable values
rows.consequence: const ROLES = ['admin', 'editor'] as const infers readonly ['admin', 'editor'] instead of string[], preserving exact literal values.

rows.means: type-safe unknown / opt-out of checking / value that can never occur
rows.consequence: Always prefer unknown over any. any disables all type checking; unknown forces you to check the type before using it.

rows.means: utility type making all properties in T optional
rows.consequence: Essential for PATCH update APIs where users can update any subset of an entity's fields without providing the entire object.

rows.means: utility type making all properties in T mandatory
rows.consequence: Inverts Partial<T>, stripping away all ? optional markers from an interface.

rows.means: utility type freezing all properties in T against mutation
rows.consequence: Marks all fields readonly, preventing accidental modifications in pure functional code pipelines.

rows.means: utility type for key-value dictionaries with keys K and values V
rows.consequence: Record<string, User> models a lookup table or hash map where string IDs map to User objects.

rows.means: utility type selecting only specified properties from T
rows.consequence: Creates a lean sub-type containing only the chosen fields, preventing leaking sensitive fields like passwords.

rows.means: utility type excluding specified properties from T
rows.consequence: Creates a new type with everything from T except the omitted keys, ideal for public DTO projections.

rows.means: extracts the return type of a function
rows.consequence: Automatically keeps types in sync when a factory function's implementation changes without needing manual type duplication.

rows.means: extracts function parameter types as a tuple
rows.consequence: Useful for wrapping or proxying third-party functions while preserving their exact argument types.

rows.means: custom function that narrows types in conditional branches
rows.consequence: function isDog(p: Animal): p is Dog { return 'bark' in p; }. Inside an if (isDog(pet)) block, pet is automatically typed as Dog.

rows.means: union of types sharing a common literal tag property
rows.consequence: Switching on the kind property lets the compiler exhaustively narrow the shape in each switch case.

rows.means: enables all strict type checking flags
rows.consequence: Turns on noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, and strictFunctionTypes, catching the vast majority of silent JavaScript bugs at build time.
